documents.title: Interleukin-6 trans-signalling drives synovial inflammation in rheumatoid arthritis
documents.text_passage: Interleukin-6 (IL-6) is a pleiotropic cytokine that contributes to the pathogenesis of rheumatoid arthritis (RA). In inflamed synovium, IL-6 activates Janus kinase/signal transducer and activator of transcription (JAK/STAT3) signalling, promotes T helper 17 cell differentiation, supports B cell differentiation and autoantibody production, and induces hepatic C-reactive protein synthesis. IL-6 also drives osteoclast differentiation, linking inflammation to joint erosion. IL-6 receptor blockade reduces C-reactive protein and acute phase reactants, and improves tender and swollen joint counts. Conclusion: IL-6 is a central pro-inflammatory cytokine in the immunopathology of rheumatoid arthritis and a validated therapeutic target.
documents.note: Illustrative record for offline demonstration only.

documents.title: IL-6 receptor blockade with tocilizumab in rheumatoid arthritis: efficacy and safety
documents.text_passage: Randomised controlled trials of tocilizumab, a humanised anti-interleukin-6 receptor antibody, in patients with moderate to severe rheumatoid arthritis show improved American College of Rheumatology response rates, reduced disease activity scores, and inhibition of radiographic progression when combined with methotrexate. Common adverse events include infection, elevation of liver enzymes and a rise in LDL cholesterol. IL-6 receptor inhibition reduces fatigue and morning stiffness. Findings across trials are broadly consistent, and meta-analyses report a favourable benefit-risk profile in patients with inadequate response to conventional synthetic disease-modifying drugs.

documents.title: Systematic review and meta-analysis of IL-6 pathway inhibitors in rheumatoid arthritis
documents.text_passage: We systematically reviewed 24 randomised trials (n = 11,472) of IL-6 pathway inhibition in rheumatoid arthritis. IL-6 inhibition increased ACR20 response compared with placebo (risk ratio 2.1, 95% CI 1.8-2.4) and reduced DAS28 scores. Serious infection rates were modestly increased. Heterogeneity was low for efficacy outcomes and moderate for safety outcomes. The evidence base is consistent: IL-6 signalling blockade is efficacious in RA, although long-term safety data remain limited and cardiovascular risk requires monitoring.

documents.title: Serum 25-hydroxyvitamin D and cancer incidence: a prospective cohort study
documents.text_passage: In a prospective cohort of 38,000 adults followed for a median of 9 years, higher serum 25-hydroxyvitamin D concentrations were associated with lower total cancer incidence in age-adjusted models (hazard ratio 0.92 per 25 nmol/L, 95% CI 0.86-0.99). The association was attenuated after adjustment for body mass index and smoking (hazard ratio 0.96, 95% CI 0.89-1.03). Results were inconsistent across cancer sites and residual confounding cannot be excluded. Observational associations do not establish that vitamin D supplementation prevents cancer.

documents.title: Vitamin D3 supplementation and cancer prevention: randomised trial results
documents.text_passage: In this randomised, placebo-controlled trial of 25,871 participants, vitamin D3 supplementation (2000 IU daily) did not significantly reduce the incidence of invasive cancer over a median follow-up of 5.3 years (hazard ratio 0.96, 95% CI 0.88-1.06). No reduction was observed for colorectal cancer or breast cancer. These findings conflict with observational reports of lower cancer risk at higher vitamin D status, suggesting that confounding explains much of the observational association. Absolute risk differences were small and the trial was not powered to detect site-specific effects.

documents.title: Citrus fruit consumption and cancer risk: pooled analysis of observational studies
documents.text_passage: Pooled analyses of observational studies report weak and inconsistent associations between citrus fruit intake and cancer risk. Some case-control studies suggest a lower risk of gastric and oesophageal cancer with higher citrus intake, whereas prospective cohorts generally show little or no association after adjustment for smoking, alcohol and socioeconomic status. No study has examined whether a daily glass of orange juice prevents cancer, and no dietary exposure has been shown to guarantee the absence of cancer. Dietary patterns are one of many interacting risk factors.

documents.title: Omega-3 fatty acids and cardiovascular outcomes: conflicting evidence from randomised trials and meta-analyses
documents.text_passage: Randomised trials of omega-3 supplementation for cardiovascular prevention have produced inconsistent results. Earlier open-label trials reported reduced cardiovascular mortality, whereas larger contemporary placebo-controlled trials found no significant reduction in major adverse cardiovascular events (hazard ratio 0.97, 95% CI 0.93-1.01). A subsequent meta-analysis suggested a small reduction in myocardial infarction with high-dose icosapent ethyl, but not with low-dose mixed omega-3 preparations. The literature therefore remains conflicting and the effect is likely to depend on dose, formulation and baseline cardiovascular risk.

documents.title: CRISPR-Cas9 genome editing in human embryos: off-target effects and long-term safety unknowns
documents.text_passage: Genome editing of human embryos with CRISPR-Cas9 has been performed in a small number of experimental studies. Reported outcomes include mosaicism, unintended large deletions and rearrangements at the target locus, and incomplete assessment of off-target edits. Because long-term health consequences of germline edits cannot be evaluated in existing follow-up periods, the long-term health effects remain unknown. Scientific bodies have called for a moratorium on heritable genome editing for reproductive purposes pending safety and governance frameworks.

documents.title: Exercise interventions for major depression: systematic review and meta-analysis
documents.text_passage: A systematic review of 49 randomised trials found that supervised aerobic and resistance exercise reduced depressive symptom severity compared with control conditions (standardised mean difference -0.62, 95% CI -0.79 to -0.45). Effects were larger in trials with higher supervision intensity and were maintained at short-term follow-up. Evidence quality was rated moderate to low because of risk of bias and small sample sizes. Exercise appears effective as an adjunct to usual care, although it should not be presented as a substitute for evidence-based treatment in severe depression.

documents.title: Gut microbiome composition and Parkinson's disease: a cohort analysis
documents.text_passage: Faecal microbiome sequencing in a cohort of 320 patients with Parkinson's disease and 320 matched controls showed reduced abundance of Prevotellaceae and increased Lactobacillaceae in cases. Associations persisted after adjustment for age, body mass index and constipation. Whether microbial changes precede or follow disease onset cannot be determined from cross-sectional data, and causal inference is not possible. The microbiome is therefore a candidate biomarker and mechanistic hypothesis rather than an established causal factor.

documents.title: Deep learning for chest radiograph triage: a retrospective evaluation
documents.text_passage: We developed a convolutional neural network to triage chest radiographs for urgent findings. On a held-out retrospective test set of 12,000 studies the model achieved an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.91 for pneumothorax and 0.84 for consolidation. Performance was lower in external validation and in under-represented subgroups. This is a retrospective single-health-system evaluation; prospective clinical trials are required before deployment claims can be made.

documents.title: Statin therapy and muscle symptoms: blinded randomised evidence
documents.text_passage: In a double-blind, randomised, placebo-controlled n-of-1 series, 60% of patients who reported muscle symptoms during statin therapy also reported symptoms during placebo periods. Blinded re-challenge showed that statin therapy was associated with a small increase in muscle symptom scores compared with placebo, but the nocebo effect accounted for most reported intolerance. These findings contrast with observational reports that attribute most muscle symptoms to statins and imply that open-label observational data overestimate statin intolerance.

documents.title: Interleukin 6 — Wikipedia (background)
documents.text_passage: Interleukin 6 is an interleukin that acts as both a pro-inflammatory cytokine and an anti-inflammatory myokine. It is secreted by T cells and macrophages to stimulate immune response. IL-6 is implicated in several diseases including diabetes, atherosclerosis, depression and rheumatoid arthritis. Tocilizumab is a monoclonal antibody against the interleukin-6 receptor used in rheumatoid arthritis and cytokine release syndrome.
documents.note: Background material only; cannot satisfy the scientific evidence requirement.
